title: 1978-10-10_SECTION_016_277.txt
concise_summary: PKD establishes that his 2-3-74 mystical experience is fundamentally Neoplatonic rather than Gnostic, grounding his vision of the Plasmate (Plotinus's Nous) and morphological essence-realm in the philosophical tradition of Plotinus and Plato. He develops a hierarchical metaphysics distinguishing the spatiotemporal sensible world from a non-spatial realm of Forms arranged by morphological identity, and proposes that the real world ended in Acts while our current world is a counterfeit creation maintained by diabolic deception.
key_claims: My 2-3-74 experience of ultra-abstraction from accidents to essence is ratified by Neoplatonist philosophy, specifically Plotinus's system of Nous and the Forms.
The Plasmate (Set) I experienced is identical to Plotinus's Nous (Intelligence), a non-extended realm ubiquitously present in the spatiotemporal world but normally imperceptible.
Two space-time continua millennia and miles apart can coincide and become one through morphological (essence-based) identity rather than spatiotemporal proximity.
The sensible world is arranged by spatiotemporal accident; the true metarealm is arranged morphologically by essence, following Platonist medieval realism rather than Aristotelian particularity.
My experience demonstrates that Plato's realm of Ideas exists ontologically real in Nous, validating medieval realism and the principle that universals are real.
The real world ceased at Acts; our current world is a counterfeit creation, a diabolical stratagem by Belial to prevent the Parousia and final judgment.
recurring_concepts: The Plasmate (Set)/Nous - the non-extended Intelligence realm omnipresent in sensible reality
Forms (Ideas/phylogons) - morphologically arranged universals in the Idea-realm above spatiotemporal existence
Morphological arrangement/essence vs. spatiotemporal arrangement/accident - two modes of ordering reality
Sacred time (illo tempore) - non-linear temporal mode overlaying or distinct from chronological time
Medieval realism - metaphysical position that universals are real entities, not merely conceptual abstractions
Ultra-abstraction - PKD's phenomenological leap from perception of particulars to direct apprehension of essences
Hierarchical stacking - vertical ontology of layered reality realms (sensible → morphological-sacred → essential-phylgonic)
The counterfeit world - Gnostic-inflected concept that our spatiotemporal reality is illusory/false, maintained by diabolic power
VALIS - identified here as the Nous itself, the actualized metaphysical realm PKD experienced
people_entities: Philip K. Dick - author reflecting on his own mystical experience
Plotinus - 3rd century Neoplatonist philosopher, primary framework for Dick's metaphysical system
Plato - ancient Greek philosopher whose theory of Forms serves as foundational model
Aristotle - Greek philosopher whose rejection of two-level reality contrasted with Plato/Plotinus
Meister Eckehart - medieval mystic; Dick cites his God/Godhead distinction as parallel to Plotinus's Nous/One
Mircea Eliade - historian of religion whose concept of illo tempore (sacred non-linear time) supports Dick's framework
Pat Warrick - scholar/critic (likely of Dick's work) mentioned for her observation about quantum mechanics
Belial - theological demon figure representing the diabolical power maintaining the counterfeit world
E.B. Macro - author of article on 'The History of Western Philosophy' quoted on Plato's realm of Ideas
Christ - figure of the third epoch of Torah (mercy), whose return/Parousia is delayed or prevented
texts_works: Plato's Parmenides - dialogue on how one Idea can be present in many particulars
Plato's Republic or theory of Forms - foundational text on the realm of Ideas
E.B. Macro, 'The History of Western Philosophy' - contemporary source on Platonic metaphysics
Encyclopedia of Philosophy (E. of Ph.) - reference work on universals and Platonic epistemology
The Torah/Hebrew Bible - framework of three epochs (justice/severity, mercy/Christ, apocalypse)
The Book of Acts - represents the frozen boundary between real and counterfeit worlds in PKD's cosmology
autobiographical: During the last few days before this entry, PKD experienced a perceptual breakthrough confirming his Set/Ground Neoplatonic metastructure insight from 3-74.
PKD's 2-3-74 (March 2-3, 1974) mystical experience involved ultra-abstraction from accidents to essence, now identified as anamnesis (Platonic recollection).
PKD's entire intellectual life for decades, his 10-volume meta-novel plus stories, articles, and letters, has epistemology as its true subject.
PKD has been puzzled for 6.5 years about where the abstract metakosmos of reticulated phylgons (the Nous) is located.
PKD's experience contradicts his sense of contemporary philosophy's explanatory capacity; contemporary philosophy 'makes no sense' to him.
PKD reports internal conflict: does he hold Kantian phenomenology, Eastern (Brahmanist) worldviews, Buddhist idealism, or medieval Christian realism?
theological_motifs: The three epochs of the Torah - justice (severity), mercy (Christ's rule), and the delayed or prevented apocalypse/Parousia
Parousia (Second Coming of Christ/final judgment) - apocalyptic event frozen or averted by diabolical stratagem
Gnosis/Gnosticism - secret knowledge that the sensible world is irreal; PKD claims his experience is NOT Gnostic but Neoplatonic
Medieval realism - theological/metaphysical doctrine that universals (Forms) are real existing entities in Divine Mind
Acosmism - possible theological framework questioning objective world-existence; Dick considers but doesn't commit to this
The Eucharist - invoked as concrete example of the implications of ultra-abstraction from accidents to essence
Anamnesis - Platonic 'recollection' of prenatal knowledge of universals; Dick identifies his 2-74 experience as literal anamnesis
The Godhead vs. God (Eckehart) - highest unmanifest principle vs. manifest creative intelligence, paralleling Plotinus's One vs. Nous
Belial's diabolical stratagem - supernatural deception maintaining the counterfeit world to prevent divine judgment
literary_self_ref: Ubik - PKD's novel whose Form-axes concept represents a breakthrough in ontological organization (morphological rather than spatiotemporal arrangement) and whose ending reveals the entire setting as afterlife/counterfeit realm
Maze of Death - referenced alongside Ubik as depicting drugged/sleeping mankind in an irreal world, parallel to Gnostic understanding
Dick's entire 10-volume meta-novel plus stories and articles - framed as extended epistemological investigation into how reality is organized and perceived
PKD's work is written from the standpoint of quantum mechanics yet explores archaic medieval realist worldview, creating tension between modern science and ancient metaphysics
symbols_images: The Plasmate (Set) - luminous or perceptually distinctive entity representing the non-extended Nous
The Form-axes - structural principles organizing reality morphologically rather than spatiotemporally, especially in Ubik
The two-level reality - shamanic and Platonic model of sensible world overlaid on/infused with sacred reality
The morphological arrangement (diagram in text) - hierarchical stacking showing sensible spatiotemporal → sacred illo tempore → phylgonic non-spatial realms
The freezeframe - Acts as frozen latent moment before world-annihilation, maintaining counterfeit present
The scanner - PKD's mind/consciousness as tool for testing or checking metaphysical claims
The thin rationalist modern veneer - surface layer of contemporary secular thought concealing archaic medieval realist substrate in human consciousness
tensions: PKD asserts medieval realism and Platonic Forms while also claiming his worldview is aligned with quantum mechanics, creating potential tension between ancient metaphysics and modern physics.

PKD rejects Gnosticism as the framework for his experience, insisting on Neoplatonism, yet retains Gnostic concepts (counterfeit world, diabolical deception, mankind asleep/drugged) in his final cosmology.
PKD denies belief in transcendent God, heaven, or afterlife, yet describes an ontologically superior realm (the Nous/Idea-realm) and divine judgment, blurring the line between his denials.
PKD experiences direct perception of Nous/Forms (his 2-74 episode) yet cannot account for why this perception is normally hidden or inaccessible to contemporary consciousness.
PKD frames his experience as ancient recollection (anamnesis) but also as modern breakthrough, unclear whether the Forms are eternally real or newly revealed.
The entire project assumes a 'primitive' or 'medieval' substrate in the modern psyche suddenly bursting through, raising questions about the nature of consciousness and history.
evidence_quotes: So in 3-74 the Plasmate (Set) that I saw as opposed to Ground is Plotinus' Nous (Intelligence) which is above the spatiotemporal realm; within it the Forms (phylgons) are morphologically arranged.
This is how my 'multiple tracking' (at two space-time continua) could occur; morphologically the two continua + the two me's - are essentially unitary, although not in spatiotemporal reality.
Universals are real, Plato's form world exists + is in Nous. Medieval realism is correct.

2-3-74 was a coming into full consciousness -+ control- of this worldview. My leap to full abstracting in 2-74 was an epiphany of - some archaic -probably medieval- substrate in me, bursting through the thin rationalist modern veneer.

The real world came to an end circa 45-70 C.E., an instant before the Parousia (i.e. the space-time of Acts): world qua real world was halted - frozen just before annihilation... A counterfeit world (or creation) such as the Gnostics describe replaced the real world - + this is the 'secret stolen past the angels in one's hands'.
uncertainty_flags: PKD identifies the Plasmate as Plotinus's Nous but uses both terms interchangeably; the exact nature of the Plasmate remains phenomenologically unclear (luminous entity? perceptual category? conscious being?).
The dating of the real world's end is stated as 'circa 45-70 C.E.' (the period of Acts), but this is tentative ('fantasy number') and may not represent PKD's final conviction.
PKD claims 6.5 years of puzzlement about the location of phylgons, suggesting he has not fully resolved the ontological status of the Idea-realm before this entry.
The relationship between PKD's own mystical experience and Plotinus's philosophical system is asserted as identity, but may be loose analogy or post-hoc rationalization.
PKD declares 'Gnosticism explains 2-2-74' is false, yet retains Gnostic language and concepts (counterfeit world, diabolical deception), creating potential for conceptual slippage.
The 'two me's' in multiple tracking are mentioned but not clearly defined—does PKD mean literal bilocation, temporal overlay, or phenomenological splitting?
The role of consciousness, will, and agency in perceiving or accessing the Form-realm remains underdeveloped; is anamnesis passive recall or active philosophical discipline?

raw_text: I passed out of the sphere of necessity.] "Both Intelligence + Soul are supposed to be present in the sensible world +, therefore, present in what is extended, although they themselves are not extended. Starting with the famous discussion in Plato's 'Parmenides', in which the attempt is made to explain how one idea can be present in many particulars, Plotinus tries to show that just because "Intelligence + Soul are not extended, they can be omnipresent + ubiquitous in what is extended." This refers precisely to my Set/Ground "two signal" "metastructure" "exploded" perception (3-74) insight (during the last few days) + identifies my experience as Neoplatonist + not Gnostic - nor anything else (i.e. my 4, 5 or 6 realms) (which are here; but we see only the discrete plurality of constituents.) So in 3-74 the Plasmate (Set) that I saw as opposed to Ground is Plotinus' Nous (Intelligence) which is above the spatiotemporal realm; within it the Forms (phylgons) are morphologically arranged. It is [indeed] {folder 01 - 012 folder 01 - 012} here ubiquitously in the spatiotemporal world but we can't discriminate it normally. In no way does Gnosticism account for my experience. The E.B. Macro article on "The History of Western Philosophy" says of Plato's theory of the realm of Ideas: "Without such shapes, which are copies of Ideas, there would be complete chaos, in which nothing would be recognizable. Furthermore, it is impossible to build up any system of knowledge without constantly preferring what is formed +, thus, recognizable to what is not, what is true to what is false, a sound logical conclusion to a logical fallacy, even an elegant scientific demonstration to a clumsy one; i.e., without considering the former as Good + the latter as Bad. In this sense at least, there is no such thing as value-free science." This well-states the necessity of abstracting + the enormous consequences of ultra abstracting - its relationship to flux, multiplicity, chaos vs the ability of the percipient to distinguish in this a latent or meta order. This strikes at the roots of our experience with + encounter with reality as a whole, whether reality will "be" (i.e. be experienced as) chaos entirely, partly chaos + partly order, greater order + less chaos, more unity + less multiplicity - quantum leaps, vast ones, in which whole multitudes of pluralities become Gestalted as structure; or, as in 2-74, space-time continua seemingly separated by 1000s of years + 1000s of miles are suddenly seen as identical (the same, one - not merely similar or tangent), by the utilizing of an otherwise (formerly) unsuspected [form]axis, based on the above-stated Platonist notion of a real realm of Ideas (cf "Ubik"). {folder 01 - 013 folder 01 - 013} Regarding this, the Form axes presented in "Ubik" represent a conceptual breakthrough - not about perception of world - but about world itself + how it may in fact be organized; viz: that in fact world itself may be organized by morphological identity or affinity rather than the contingent relatedness of spatiotemporality (i.e. essential not positional relatedness). There is nothing in my concept not found in Plato + Plotinus, but the Neoplatonist schools were closed in the 6th century C.E. which is a long time ago. [Note] This is how my "multiple tracking" (at two space-time continua) could occur; morphologically the two continua + the two me's - are essentially unitary, although not in spatiotemporal reality. What is pointed to is not just a higher way of apprehending, ordering, abstracting reality, but a non-spatiotemporal realm in itself, discovered by ultra abstracting perception but not created by it. The implications in this for epistemology defy description. After all, epistemology as a subdivision of metaphysics is the true topic of "Ubik", of my entire 10-volume meta novel plus stories + articles + letters - my whole intellectual life, for decades. [Note] However, Eliade goes into this with his presentation of "illo tempore" or sacred (non linear) time. But above this morphologically-arranged realm which is in some kind of time + space, although not arranged primarily by time + space, lies the abstract realm of phylgons in which there is no time + space at all - + I experienced it. {folder 01 - 014 folder 01 - 014} [illustration presented below in text form] Morphological arrangement => Morphological arrangement ----------------------------- but spatiotemporal existence, ----------------------------- creating the median realm of ------------------------------ sacred time, illo tempore, Spatiotemporal arrangement => in which two space-time ------------------------------ continua can superimpose + be one. Plotinus' distinction between Nous + the One is Eckehart's distinction between God + the Godhead. If it was just a matter of superior abstracting by the percipient, only an inner concept would come into existence; but an external, actual, morphological arrangement of reality -ontologically superior to the spatiotemporal- coincides with this ultra abstracting; therefore the practical consequences of this abstracting from accidents to essence are epistemologically enormous. Two space-time continua (1000s of miles + years apart) coincide to form (reveal) an unsuspected metarealm + structure. This is hierarchical stacking. - To sum up: Abstract from accidents to essence. Accidents are arranged in space + time; essence is arranged morphologically like the Form-axes in "Ubik", + not in space + time. So: (1) Two separate space time continua will coincide if they possess a common essence (2) A meta-realm of morphological arrangement is disclosed not utilizing space-time (3) Neoplatonism explains 2-3-74. {folder 01 - 015 folder 01 - 015} (4) Put another way, 2-3-74 demonstrates that Plotinus' system is correct. (5) The essence realm is Plato's Idea realm in contradistinction to the sensible realm (as reappraised by Plotinus), i.e. the realm of accidents (the sensible realm). Universals are real, Plato's form world exists + is in Nous. Medieval realism is correct. E of Ph on "universals": "... Because Plato's Forms do not exist at a place or at a time" [Note] ... "Particulars are only semi-real." [Note] "The mystery of their 'existence' becomes impenetrable." Where are they, if they exist? [Note2] My solution: Morphological arrangement without reference to space + time. This can only mean that Plotinus is right; the Forms exist in Nous, + I saw/experienced that Nous: Valis. [Note2] This had puzzled me for 6 1/2 years: where is the abstract metakosmos of the reticulated phylgons? [...] (Nous) {folder 01 - 016} E PH article on "Universals": The contrast between the two views (Plato's and Aristotle's) comes out again in their accounts of how we apprehend universals. They are agreed both that awareness of universals is implicit in ordinary sense experience (for it is this awareness that conditions our experience as being what it is) and that we are aware of universals not by sense itself but by intellect. Plato could not say that we became aware of them by abstraction from particular instances, because they have separate existence and never are more than defectively instantiated: if our concept of X were only what we could abstract from imperfect instances, we never could apprehend X itself. Therefore there must be some other mode of apprehension, which Plato called anamnesis (usually translated as "recollection" but less misleadingly interpreted in this context as "recovery"). The human soul has prenatal knowledge of universals and of their mutual relations, and postnatal experience of the ordinary world serves, or may serve, to revive this knowledge in suitable circumstances. Thus, experience does not directly provide us with new apprehensions (of universals) or with new knowledge of necessary truths (connections between universals) but acts as a stimulus to remind us of what we already know but have hitherto in this life forgotten... Aristotle thought that there was another, less fanciful and less speculative way... Apprehension of a universal, or formation of the concept, is not a sudden once-and-for-all business, given in a single experience, but a gradual process. (Etc. Etc.) (My comments: Plato seems to be describing exactly what happened to me in 2-74; exactly what happened, and he offers a reason as to why it happened that fits in with my general schema vis-a-vis Plotinus. So again I feel ratified in my conviction of last night that Platonism and neo-Platonism are absolutely pointed to in my "ultra abstraction" of 2-74, as I have phrased it.) My leap to full abstracting in 2-74 was an epiphany of - some archaic -probably medieval- substrate in me, bursting through the thin rationalist modern veneer. Contemporary philosophy makes no sense to me. & yet, as Pat Warrick says, I write from the standpoint of quantum mechanics. My God isn't even transcendent - No; I don't believe in heaven or an afterlife. What do I believe in? Kantian phenomenology? That an invisible latent realm exists immanently in the sensible world or that no objective world in itself exists at all? Acosmism? Something Eastern (e.g. Brahmanism?) "If you press world hard enough it yields up God" - paraphrase of p. 485. "I define God as world under the threat of death ... God forced into the open, + put to work in the service of evading death." I am not I; I am not here; I am not now. Buddhist idealism? No, because when self + world go, God -not the void- replaces them, + world is seen as an abstraction outside space + time, an interconnected system of ideas in His mind; more precisely, a memory [s...t .n] process (i.e. not static). {folder 01 - 018 folder 01 - 018} Let me run a fantasy number by my scanner. But the 3rd epoch [of the Torah] never arrived; for us, anyhow. A counterfeit world (or creation) such as the Gnostics describe replaced the real world - + this is the "secret stolen past the angels in one's hands". This is the secret gnosis of Gnosticism; they knew they were living in an irreal world, + that mankind is drugged or asleep (as in "Ubik" + "Maze"). Why is this the case? A diabolical stratagem by Belial to stave off the apocalypse, the Parousia + judgment. The spatiotemporal world is counterfeit -irreal- but under it/within it/behind it/above it/beyond it/outside it (as in "Ubik") lies the real world + it is not spatiotemporal; there is no spatiotemporal world; that ended with Acts, which is now a latent freezeframe.
